item.title: The Virtue of Laziness in an AI Enabled World
item.description: This is a great essay by Bryan Cantrill about the decline of laziness as a virtue in programming. Of course, the implicit wink here is that it takes a lot of work to be lazy: when programmers are engaged in the seeming laziness of hammock-driven development, we are in fact turning the problem over and over in our heads. We undertake the hard intellectual work of developing these abstractions in part because we are optimizing the hypothetical time of our future selves, even if at the expense of our current one.

item.title: The AI Tarpit
item.description: I’ve been noticing a trend of people sending me AI slop as insights. It’s been a slow burn, but it is increasing. A salesperson sending me obviously AI generated content, a four page value study filled with AI nonsense, a graphic portfolio of the most milquetoast content. Whatever it is, you can tell that it’s AI generated because of the cloyingly polite way it says nothing. The thing that concerns me is the frequency with which otherwise smart people are missing the fact that it says nothing.
